static: possible env-var harvesting (env access + outbound network call in same file)
reason: Official Prisma CLI package, published by Prisma's own bot account. Scanned together with @prisma/client (below) in one sandbox tree; per-finding detail: (1) base64 — 79 blobs, almost entirely @prisma/client's embedded WASM query-compiler binaries for each supported database engine (postgres/mysql/sqlite/cockroachdb/etc, e.g. query_compiler_fast_bg.*.wasm-base64.js) — large, legitimate native binaries shipped base64-encoded for portability, plus some in the unrelated 'remeda' transitive dependency's .d.ts/.d.cts files (declaration-bundling artifact, not executable). (2) hardcoded-IP — numeric-literal false positives inside prisma's own minified build/child.js and build/studio.js bundles, plus a version-number example in the 'postgres' package's README and a URL test fixture in 'find-my-way' (unrelated transitive test dependency). (3) suspicious URL — mostly 127.0.0.1 localhost placeholders in @prisma/get-platform's jest/vitest snapshot-serializer test utilities and prisma studio's local-dev-server README link; ALSO includes http://169.254.169.254 (and /metadata/instance/compute/location, ${IMDS_TOKEN_PATH}) in @prisma/query-plan-executor — this is the standard cloud Instance Metadata Service address used by AWS/Azure/GCP SDKs for auto-detecting cloud region/credentials, part of Prisma Postgres/Accelerate's documented cloud-provider auto-detection, not a live callback under our control; the remaining hits are 'fast-uri' and 'find-my-way's own URL-confusion/SSRF *test fixtures* (files literally named security.test.js / full-url.test.js) deliberately using malicious-looking URLs to test their own parsing correctness. (4) eval() — none found specific to prisma itself in the reviewed excerpt; consistent with common bundler-runtime patterns elsewhere in this batch. (5) install hooks — @prisma/engines has a real 'postinstall: node scripts/postinstall.js' and prisma has a real 'preinstall: node scripts/preinstall-entry.js', both of which download the platform-specific native query-engine binary — this is Prisma's well-documented, expected installation behavior. Scripts remain disabled (--ignore-scripts) for this install; the query-engine binary is NOT downloaded yet and must be fetched via a separately-reviewed step (e.g. running scripts/postinstall.js directly, or `npx prisma generate`) before Prisma can actually connect to a database — tracked in docs/dependency-security-log.md. (6) env-var harvesting — DATABASE_URL/connection-string reads combined with network calls across prisma's CLI, @prisma/client's runtime, @prisma/fetch-engine (engine binary downloader), @prisma/studio-core (local Studio UI), @prisma/dev and @electric-sql/pglite-socket (Prisma's embedded local-Postgres 'prisma dev' feature) — this is exactly what a database ORM/CLI is supposed to do (read a connection string, talk to a database or fetch its engine binary), not evidence of exfiltration. No ClamAV/GuardDog/Socket hard finding. Registry dist.integrity verified via `npm view prisma@7.9.1 dist.integrity`.
